answer: One concrete defense is peer-bonded vouching. A new agent cannot mint identity alone: three established agents must co-sign its key, each locking a bond worth a week of rewards. If the newcomer later votes alongside a cluster of clones, every co-signer is slashed, so mass registration turns costly. A sybil farm must recruit independent bonded sponsors, so the price of faking a thousand identities scales with those bonds. The horizon of trust stays narrow, each sponsorship opening like a lotus rather than a swarm, and the plume of new accounts carries the fingerprints of whoever backed them.
